assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
Period: 18 to 31 Oct 2026 compared with 4 to 17 Oct 2026 (the immediately preceding period of equal length), since no period was specified in the question.
caveats: Duplicate records on 12 Oct: 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts, +3.0%). Paysight counts each attempt once, keeping the first ingestion.

Attempt volume from 18 to 31 Oct was about 39% above the usual level for those weekdays. Sales and data gaps both look like this, so check before comparing totals across this period. It is not a data error by itself.
Success rate depends on the denominator: 88.5% by attempts, 90.9% by orders and 92.1% technical. Retries and customer drop-offs explain the gap.
Failure codes are quoted per 100 attempts for Harbor Bank debit cards only, not for all traffic.
The daily trend for Harbor Bank debit shown covers only the baseline days (4 to 15 Oct), so it does not show the day-by-day onset of the drop in the current window.

facts.text: Attempt success rate fell 1.47pp from 90.0% to 88.5%. Attempts rose from 165,297 to 230,100. The change is statistically significant (p = 1.12e-48) and the confidence intervals do not overlap (baseline 89.9%–90.2%, current 88.4%–88.7%).
By payment method, the -1.47pp splits into a mix effect of -1.00pp (68.0% of the change) and a rate effect of -0.47pp.
CARD_EMI's share of attempts rose from 2.9% to 10.9% while its own success rate was flat (81.7% to 81.6%). It carries a mix effect of -0.61pp. Its rate is well below the 90.0% overall baseline.
UPI's share fell from 54.0% to 42.5% at a steady rate (93.1% to 93.0%), a mix effect of -0.43pp because UPI is one of the higher-success methods.
NovaMart's share of attempts grew from 6.0% to 30.0%. It accounts for -0.96pp (65%) of the -1.47pp change, and its own rate fell from 90.0% to 86.2%.
Within payment methods, the largest like-for-like drop is Harbor Bank debit cards: success rate fell 9.44pp from 86.2% to 76.7%, contributing -0.39pp to the overall change.
For Harbor Bank debit cards, ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE rose from 0.32 to 11.12 per 100 attempts (22 to 1,065 failures). Other failure codes were broadly flat or slightly lower.
Harbor Bank debit daily success rate stayed between roughly 84% and 89% across the baseline days shown, so the baseline was stable.
The success rate depends on the denominator: 88.5% by attempts, 90.9% by orders, and 92.1% technical (excluding customer drop-offs).

response.headline: Attempt success rate fell 1.47pp, from 90.0% to 88.5% (18–31 Oct vs 4–17 Oct). About two-thirds of the fall (-1.00pp) comes from a shift in payment-method mix, driven by NovaMart's growth and more EMI volume; the remaining -0.47pp is a like-for-like rate drop, concentrated in Harbor Bank debit cards.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Break CARD_EMI and payment-method share down by merchant within NovaMart, and confirm with the business whether a sale or EMI offer started on or around 18 Oct.
hypotheses.rationale: NovaMart's share jumped from 6.0% to 30.0% in the same window as CARD_EMI's share rose from 2.9% to 10.9%, and overall volume was about 39% above usual. EMI's own rate did not change.
hypotheses.text: The NovaMart ramp-up (likely a sale or campaign) pushed more traffic into EMI and credit card, which have lower success rates, creating most of the mix-driven decline.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Ask Harbor Bank whether risk rules or thresholds changed from 18 Oct, and check whether the declines cluster on NovaMart or particular merchant categories, amounts or BIN ranges.
hypotheses.rationale: ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE rose from 0.32 to 11.12 per 100 attempts for Harbor Bank debit while other failure codes stayed flat, which points to an issuer-side decision rather than a technical fault. Harbor Bank's own volume also rose (share 8.8% to 11.0%), so a risk model reacting to the traffic is possible.
hypotheses.text: Harbor Bank began applying stricter risk rules to debit card transactions in the current window, causing the surge in risk declines.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check whether NovaMart is an enterprise merchant in the electronics category, and re-run the driver ranking excluding NovaMart.
hypotheses.rationale: Enterprise (-1.08pp) and electronics (-0.52pp) both grew sharply in share and fell in rate over the same window as NovaMart's growth, but the evidence does not link NovaMart to those tiers directly.
hypotheses.text: Part of the like-for-like drop in the 'enterprise' merchant tier and in electronics reflects NovaMart's traffic rather than separate problems.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Harbor Bank began applying stricter risk rules to debit card transactions in the current window
recommendations.rationale: This is the single largest identified like-for-like drop (-9.44pp within the segment) and is plausibly recoverable by the issuer.
recommendations.text: Raise the Harbor Bank debit ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE spike with Harbor Bank and request the reason codes and any rule changes since 18 Oct.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: By payment method, the -1.47pp splits into a mix effect of -1.00pp (68.0% of the change) and a rate effect of -0.47pp.
recommendations.rationale: Most of the headline decline is a mix effect that does not reflect a worse like-for-like service; blended rates will keep looking weaker while this traffic stays high.
recommendations.text: Report success rate for NovaMart and for CARD_EMI separately from the blended figure, and compare each to its own baseline.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: NovaMart's share of attempts grew from 6.0% to 30.0%. It accounts for -0.96pp (65%) of the -1.47pp change, and its own rate fell from 90.0% to 86.2%.
recommendations.rationale: NovaMart drives 65% of the overall change, and the evidence shows its rate fell as well as its share rising.
recommendations.text: Investigate why NovaMart's own success rate fell from 90.0% to 86.2%, starting with its payment-method and issuer mix and failure codes.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: The NovaMart ramp-up (likely a sale or campaign) pushed more traffic into EMI and credit card, which have lower success rates
recommendations.rationale: EMI's low rate and rising share together create a structural drag on the blended rate during promotions.
recommendations.text: Confirm with the business whether a sale or EMI promotion started around 18 Oct, and consider whether EMI success can be improved given its low rate (about 81.6%).
